name: Single-Packet Attack (HTTP/2 Race Conditions)
command: # Turbo Intruder: engine=Engine.BURP2, requests sent with gate='race1'
description: Exploits race conditions by eliminating network jitter so many requests reach the server within the same ~1ms window. Uses the HTTP/2 single-packet attack (up to ~20-30 requests in one TCP packet) or HTTP/1.1 last-byte synchronization to overrun limit/coupon/balance/one-time-use logic (limit-overrun and multi-endpoint race variants). Driven with Burp's Turbo Intruder and the Repeater 'send group in parallel' feature.
source: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - Race conditions
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  Many checks (is this coupon used? is balance >= amount?) read state, then write it, without a lock. If N requests pass the read before any write lands (TOCTOU), all N succeed. The attack removes jitter so the requests hit the critical window simultaneously.

=== SINGLE-PACKET ATTACK (HTTP/2) ===
  - Send up to ~20-30 requests whose last frame is withheld, then release all final frames in ONE TCP packet. Server processes them with near-zero timing spread.
  - Immune to network jitter (unlike the old 'last-byte sync' over many connections).

=== LAST-BYTE SYNC (HTTP/1.1 fallback) ===
  - Open N connections, send all but the final byte of each request, then send the last bytes together.

=== BURP REPEATER (quick test) ===
  - Add the request to a Repeater tab group.
  - Group dropdown > 'Send group in parallel (single-packet attack)'.
  - Good for 2-50 identical requests (coupon redeem, gift-card apply, vote).

=== TURBO INTRUDER (programmatic) ===
  def queueRequests(target, wordlists):
      engine = RequestEngine(endpoint=target.endpoint, concurrentConnections=1, engine=Engine.BURP2)
      for i in range(20):
          engine.queue(target.req, gate='race1')
      engine.openGate('race1')
  def handleResponse(req, interesting):
      table.add(req)

=== TARGETS ===
  - Redeem a single-use coupon/gift card many times.
  - Withdraw/transfer more than the balance (limit overrun).
  - Bypass rate limits / anti-brute-force counters.
  - Multi-endpoint races (e.g. apply-then-confirm).

examples.label: Repeater: send a tab group in parallel
examples.command: Burp Repeater > group tab > 'Send group in parallel (single-packet attack)'

examples.label: Open the gate to release all withheld final frames

recommended.note: Repeater's 'send group in parallel' is the quickest single-packet test.

defense.why_it_works: State-changing operations read a value (coupon unused, balance sufficient) and write the new value without holding a lock across the check. The single-packet attack collapses the timing spread so many requests pass the read phase before any write commits (a TOCTOU window).
defense.prerequisites: An endpoint whose outcome depends on shared mutable state with no atomic guard (uniqueness constraint, row lock, or idempotency key). HTTP/2 support helps but HTTP/1.1 last-byte sync also works.
defense.impact: Limit/coupon/gift-card/balance overrun, bypass of one-time-use and rate-limit controls, duplicate order or withdrawal, and other business-logic integrity loss.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Bursts of near-identical requests to the same state-changing endpoint from one client within a few milliseconds, repeated 2xx on an action that should succeed at most once, and HTTP/2 flows releasing many stream END_STREAM frames together.
defense.artifacts: Reverse-proxy/app access logs with millisecond timestamps showing clustered identical POSTs, application logs showing the same coupon/transaction id applied multiple times, and WAF rate counters.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web uri_path="/redeem" method=POST
| bin _time span=1s
| stats count by _time, clientip, uri_path
| where count>3
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem == "/redeem" and csMethod == "POST"
| summarize reqs=count() by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1s)
| where reqs > 3
defense.prevention: Make state changes atomic: database uniqueness constraints, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / row locks, or idempotency keys per operation. Serialize per-resource critical sections. Do not rely on an initial read-check; enforce the invariant at commit time. Treat rate limits as best-effort, not security.

detections.name: Burst of identical state-changing POSTs within 1 second
detections.logic:
index=web method=POST (uri_path="/redeem" OR uri_path="/transfer" OR uri_path="/apply-coupon")
| bin _time span=1s
| stats count as reqs by _time, clientip, uri_path
| where reqs>3
detections.false_positives: Legitimate client retries, double-click submits, and mobile apps that batch requests.
detections.tuning: Scope to endpoints that must be idempotent/one-time; correlate with repeated use of the same coupon/transaction id in app logs.
